title: RF-DETR-N vs YOLOX-M: benchmark on one protocol
dek: Measured on the same COCO protocol at each model's default input: accuracy ties at 51.4 vs 51.7 mAP, and which one is faster depends entirely on the runtime.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: Accuracy is a tie: RF-DETR-N and YOLOX-M land at 51.4 vs 51.7 mAP@50-95 on an RTX 5070 Ti in PyTorch. The two run at different input sizes, RF-DETR-N at 384 px and YOLOX-M at 640 px, each at its author default. On this GPU YOLOX-M is 18% faster, but that lead reverses on ONNX Runtime, Jetson Orin, and Raspberry Pi 5. RF-DETR-N also uses less peak VRAM at 151 vs 172 MB.

RF-DETR-N (30.47M parameters, Apache-2.0) runs at 384 px input, while YOLOX-M (25.33M, Apache-2.0) runs at 640 px. Each figure is the author default, so this is a comparison of shipped configurations, not a matched-resolution test. Both were evaluated on COCO val2017 with verified rows on desktop GPU, Jetson Orin, and Raspberry Pi 5.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017. RF-DETR-N and YOLOX-M highlighted against the full set of measured models.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent form. RF-DETR-N measures 51.4 mAP@50-95 and YOLOX-M 51.7, close enough to call a tie. The one row that separates them is small objects: YOLOX-M leads 32.9 vs 27.7 mAP_small, a 15.9% relative gap. At 640 px, YOLOX-M keeps more small-object detail.

On the RTX 5070 Ti, YOLOX-M is 18.0% faster in PyTorch (48.2 vs 39.5 FPS). That is the only setting where it wins. On ONNX Runtime RF-DETR-N leads 65.7 vs 55.8 FPS, on Jetson Orin 10.2 vs 9.1 FPS, and on Raspberry Pi 5 2.1 vs 0.8 FPS.
The speed answer here is not portable. YOLOX-M wins only on desktop PyTorch; RF-DETR-N is faster on ONNX Runtime, Jetson Orin, and Raspberry Pi 5. Benchmark on your own runtime before choosing.

Pick RF-DETR-N for edge and CPU targets like Jetson Orin or Raspberry Pi 5, where it is faster, and when peak VRAM matters at 151 vs 172 MB. Pick YOLOX-M for desktop PyTorch throughput or when small-object recall at 640 px is the priority. Both ship under Apache-2.0, so licensing does not force the choice.

# pip install libreyolo
from libreyolo import LibreYOLO

rfdetr = LibreYOLO("LibreRFDETRn.pt") # 384 px, 51.4 mAP@50-95
yolox = LibreYOLO("LibreYOLOXm.pt")   # 640 px, 51.7 mAP@50-95

results = rfdetr("image.jpg")
